findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed no sanitizer solution to be available upon arrival. Discussed with PIC, sanitizer solution was made and prepared at 200 ppm Quat. Ensure a sanitizer solution is prepared and available during all hours of operation.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed microwave to have food splash accumulation on the inside roof of microwave. Discussed with PIC, microwave will be cleaned. Ensure facility is cleaning microwave at a frequency that prevents food splash accumulation.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed dirty mop bucket to be kept in facility over night. Discussed with PIC, bucket will disposed of. Ensure staff is properly disposing of mop water after mopping.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.113 Storing Maintenance Tools. Maintenance tools such as brooms, mops, vacuum cleaners, and similar items shall be: (A) Stored so they do not contaminate FOOD, EQUIPMENT, UTENSILS, LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES; and (B) Stored in an orderly manner that facilitates cleaning the area used for storing the maintenance tools.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
2-201.11: (A) The PERMIT HOLDER shall require FOOD EMPLOYEES and CONDITIONAL EMPLOYEES to report to the PERSON IN CHARGE information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through FOOD. Report: Symptoms (all P except lesion), diagnosis (all P), and possible exposures (P).  (E) Responsibility of food employee to report symptoms/disease to PIC. 

Observed no signed employee health reporting agreements. Discussed with PIC. Provided copy of the agreement. Ensure all employees read and sign the document. Ensure new hires read and sign the document as a part of onboarding. Keep copies in the public health binder. Inspector will follow-up on 5/12/23.

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.comment:
2-501.11: A FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall have written procedures for EMPLOYEES to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT. The procedures shall address the specific actions EMPLOYEES must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of EMPLOYEES, consumers, FOOD, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter. Reference 2-501.11.  

Observed no way to clean vomit/diarrhea in a manner that will kill for Norovirus. Facility had the policy that SCDPH utilizes posted on the wall near the office desk; however, the facility has no bleach to perform this procedure. PIC was not sure if Subway will let the facility have bleach in the building. Discussed purchasing a biohazard clean-up kit as an alternative. Inspector will follow-up on 5/12/23.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the active sani bucket in the sandwich prep area to be 100 ppm of quaternary ammonium when tested with test strips. Discussed with PIC. PIC remade the sani bucket - 400 ppm. Ensure sani buckets are remade as frequently as needed to maintain a concentration of 200-400 ppm for quaternary ammonium. Facility has test strips to confirm concentration levels. Utilize test strips to check concentrations. COS.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

(REPEAT) Observed no hanging thermometers in the walk-in cooler and the prep table coolers. Discussed with PIC. Ensure facility has extra thermometers on hand and all cold holding units have a thermometer in each unit. The digital reading outside coolers will not suffice alone. Ensure thermometers are placed in the coolers. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 4/22/22.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-302.12: (A) FOOD TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of FOOD temperatures. (B) A TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE with a suitable small diameter probe that is designed to measure the temperature of thin masses shall be provided and readily accessible to accurately measure the temperature in thin FOODS such as MEAT patties and FISH filets. 

Observed no probe style thermometer for the facility. Discussed with PIC. Ensure a probe thermometer is purchased. Inspector will follow-up on 5/12/23.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.16: (A) Wall and ceiling covering materials shall be attached so that they are EASILY CLEANABLE. (B) Except in areas used only for dry storage, concrete, porous blocks, or bricks used for indoor wall construction shall be finished and SEALED to provide a SMOOTH, nonabsorbent, EASILY CLEANABLE surface. 

Observed the following areas in need of re-caulking:
1. Mop sink in the back has moldy caulk along the basin.
2. Three compartment sink has moldy caulking sealing the equipment to the wall.
3. Men’s bathroom hand sink has moldy caulking sealing the sink to the wall.

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure all three areas are re-caulked so the mold is new and not moldy. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

Chili is observed in the steam well next to the hand sink in the prep area at 80 degrees F. Investigation showed that the steam well was not on. The chili was discarded by PIC immediately and the steam well turned on to correct.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

On arrival, both prep coolers on the make line are observed with TCS foods in the 45-53 degree (F) range (probed). A discussion took place in relation to the procedures and temperatures related to the coolers with the PIC. Temperatures are taken as the facility is opening (9ish) and again in the afternoon (6ish). Logs for the coolers show acceptable temperatures up to and including this morning. It is observed warm in the facility today and PIC noted that the back AC unit for the facility has been out for several weeks. The owner has bids out for a replacement, but the PIC has not been given a timeframe for the replacement to take place. The lids to the coolers were open as the inspection took place. PIC stated that the foods had mostly been cycled in the past hour or less, and items that were from a half hour or less are showing acceptable temperature ranges. All other TCS foods were moved into the walk in freezer for rapid cooling and the lids of the units closed after thermometer were placed in them (refer to violation #36). Temperatures were observed at 37 prior to inspection conclusion. Foods were brought from the walk in cooler as needed for service. Coolers currently appear to be working correctly. PIC stated that they would monitor the foods in the coolers over the weekend to ensure safety limits are maintained. Inspector will spot check next week to verify the same.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. 

The following maintenance repairs remain from the pre-opening inspection: 1) caulking soda fountain station in the lobby to the wall; 2) repair damaged wall tile to the left of the stool in the men’s rooms.
